room-plan.title: The room plan
room-plan.summary: The space where the occasion takes place, to scale. Seating and the fit checks start from here. You can also draw it exactly, with walls and corners to scale.
room-plan.keywords: room plan floor plan space dimensions venue drawing scale width length version cad walls corners snap grid angle rectangle L-shape door pillar measure stage dance floor dancers

body.p1: If you added the venue from the business directory to your suppliers and it has published approved plans, you see them here.

ol1.b: Under “Use the venue's plan”, press the button with the name of the plan you want.
ol1.c: The plan enters the occasion at its current version, together with the venue's tables.

body.note1: If the venue changes its plan later, you receive a proposal. Your plan stays at its version until you accept the change. Nothing changes by itself.

ol2.a: Type the “Name of the space”, for example “Grandparents' courtyard”.
ol2.b: Fill in “Width (m)” and “Length (m)”. Leave them empty if you do not know them yet.

body.note2: Missing dimensions are shown as “unknown” and are not guessed. Without them, the fit check tells you honestly that it does not know whether the tables fit.
body.p2: Under “What we know about the space” you find what the venue has stated. The plan to scale can be printed from “Print and export”.
body.pDraw: A space you described yourself can be drawn exactly: press “Draw the room”.

olDraw1.a: “Rectangle”: click two opposite corners, or type the width and depth.
olDraw1.b: “Walls”: click each corner in turn, or type a “Length (m)” and a direction. Close on the first corner.
olDraw1.c: “Select”: drag corners, or type a wall's exact length. “Add a corner in the middle” makes an L-shaped room.

body.noteDraw1: Snapping to the grid, corners and 15° angles can be turned off. The keys are listed under the drawing.
body.pDraw2: Press “Save drawing”. Tables stay where they were; the fit check shows if any ended up outside the room.
body.noteDraw3: “Door” and “Pillar” place doors and pillars; the floor in front of a door stays clear. “Measure” shows the distance between two points.

seating.title: Seating at tables
seating.summary: You put tables on the plan and guests at tables. You can drag with a finger or use the buttons: both do the same thing.
seating.keywords: seating tables seats plan guests not seated fits stages dancing publish your seat
seating.need: The owner and project managers. You need a room plan first.

ol1.a: Open “Seating”. If you have no plan yet, you are sent to “Room plan”.
ol1.b: Press “Add a table” and choose one of the venue's tables or describe one of your own.
ol1.c: Move the table by dragging it on the plan or, without dragging, open it and type the position, then press “Move here”.
ol1.d: Tap a table in the list or on the plan, tick who sits at it and press “Seat at the table”.
ol1.e: Watch the “Not seated” list until it reaches zero.

body.note1: The fit check says “It fits”, that it does not fit, or “Unknown”. If we do not know the room's dimensions or how many seats a table has, we do not guess.
body.p1: Under “Stages” you can press “Add the usual stages”. Each stage has its own arrangement and its own check: for example, for dancing you take a few tables out with “Put away in this stage”. The base arrangement stays the same.
body.p2: Under “What guests see”, press “Show guests their seat”. Each guest sees their table (and seat, if you chose one) on their link. “Hide the seating again” takes it back.
body.note2: Nobody sees other people's names. Until you publish, guests see nothing of the seating.
body.p3: A seating layout proposed by an AI assistant appears first as a preview in “What if?”.
body.noteTables: Under “Add a table”, pick a “Ready-made table”: round, square, rectangular, oval, half-moon or cocktail, in common hire sizes with the number of chairs filled in. You can change anything afterwards.
body.noteTools: “Measure” shows the distance between tables. “Reference people” puts people to scale on the plan; “Fill the dance floor with dancers” shows a full floor. “Ready-made item” has stages, dance floors, speakers and lighting. Stages, dance floors and live bands resize with the ↔ and ↕ buttons or by dragging the square at the corner.

stationery.title: Invitations and stationery
stationery.summary: You choose a design, adjust the wording and see the proof at once. What you see is exactly what gets printed.
stationery.keywords: invitations stationery design proof pdf print printer version bleed crop marks digital collection embroidery weaving rustic traditional palette starter wording
stationery.need: The planning team can work on the wording. Only the organisers can mark the proof as checked.

ol1.a: Open “Invitations”, choose a collection (“Made for this occasion” — 52 templates drawn for your kind of occasion —, the house designs, Romanian embroidery and weaving, the signature collection, rustic, traditional or all compositions), then a design and a colourway, and adjust the wording. “Starter wording” fills in a ready-made text for your kind of occasion. The proof changes at once, before you save.
ol1.b: Press “Save version”. Every save is a new version.
ol1.c: Press “Download the proof (PDF)” and read it word by word: names, date, time, address.
ol1.d: If everything is correct, press “I have checked the proof”.
ol1.e: Press “Download the print PDF” and send the file to the printer. If they ask for it, tick “Add crop marks”.

body.note1: The print PDF can be made only for a version you have read and marked as checked. If you change one word, you save a new version and check it again.
body.p1: The file has the exact format, 3 mm bleed, vector text and embedded fonts. Colours are RGB; the printer converts to CMYK.
body.p2: Under “The digital invitation”, press “Use on the guests' link” so that each household's link carries the same words and the same colours as the printed invitation. “Go back to the standard invitation” undoes it.
body.p3: “Print and export” also has invitations with a QR code, one sheet per household, labels with codes and table cards.
